title: F02 — Auth
tagline: Sign in with Apple or email next to Continue offline; every backend call carries a fresh ID token; the account can be deleted.
intro: Sprint S1 · 21h · skeleton guide — full code is added when this feature starts.
Code in this guide is a teaching example. Check current source and follow F00 localization rules before applying it.

sections.title: 5. Local — Firebase Auth inside the data source

blocks.html:
Overview

  • Goal: AuthRemoteDataSourceImpl keeps its type and methods; inside it calls Firebase. AccountRemoteDataSourceImpl calls the backend through HTTPClient.
ActionFileHolds
Editproject.ymlfirebase-ios-sdk (FirebaseAuth), Sign in with Apple capability; run xcodegen
EditApp/AppDelegate.swiftFirebaseApp.configure() first
NewPlatformKit/Networking/HTTPClient.swiftBase URL, token provider, one 401 interceptor that refreshes once
ReplaceDataSources/Remote/Auth/AuthRemoteDataSourceImpl.swiftFirebase Apple and email sign-in, current user, sign out, ID token
ReplaceDataSources/Remote/Account/AccountRemoteDataSourceImpl.swiftDELETE /account through HTTPClient
EditApp/DI/PlatformDI.swift, DataSourcesDI.swiftRegister HTTPClient, pass it in; registered types stay
  • Check: real Apple and email sign-in on device; airplane-mode relaunch after sign-in goes straight in; repository and view models unchanged.

Steps

  1. getIDToken(forcingRefresh: false) per request; never store the token yourself.
  2. Ten requests that all get 401 cause one refresh, not ten.
  3. Sign out clears nothing local: offline data stays on the device.
